newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Office Depot again draws crowd.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Office Depot again draws crowd.

text.p: Office Depot Inc options continued to attract heavy interest before a judge's decision on its proposed merger with Staples Inc, traders said Monday.
U.S. District Judge Thomas Hogan will hand down his decision on the $4 billion merger at 1630 EDT/2030 GMT, a clerk of the court said.
Last Friday, as word spread that a decision on the deal would be forthcoming, some investors made sizable bets that Office Depot shares would fall sharply on the news.
But on Monday, it appeared that some bullish bets were being made.
Office Depot options activity was led by the July 20 calls, which traded about 8,640 contracts. The July 17-1/2 call traded 5,815 and the July 22-1/2 call traded 3,370.
"Hope springs eternal," said Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co.
The busiest Office Depot put was the July 15, which traded about 1,065 contracts.
The U.S. Federal Trade Commission is seeking to block the office superstores' merger, arguing the combination would lead to higher prices for consumers.
A five-day hearing was held before Judge Hogan in May.
Office Depot shares were unchanged at 19-5/16 in late trading on Monday.
Options on Office Depot have been extremely busy over the last couple of weeks, and volatilities in the options have been steady at high levels, traders said.
According to Lawrence McMillan, publisher of the Daily Volume Alert, volume in Office Depot options last Friday surged to 90,444 contracts from an average of 26,269.
Average volatility in the Office Depot July options ranged from 122 to about 150. In the August series, it hovered around 100, and in the Octobers it ranged from around 73 to 89.
In other trading, a straddle in Occidental Petroleum Corp July 30s crossed. The July 30 call and put each traded 5,000 contracts.
The Occidental January 30 call traded 2,145 contracts.
